fact_check_log.claim: Shinto ceremony in kimono typically followed by a Christian-style observance in Western attire (intro, section 5, FAQ)
Arranged marriage largely replaced by love match; nakodo go-between still common
Traditional ceremony at a Shinto shrine; white under-kimono and shiromuku
Bride changes into a brightly coloured kimono for the reception; red brocade uchikake with cranes, symbols of longevity
Uchikake now worn only by brides; outfit changes continue; colour alteration can include a Western gown
Merchant-class black uchikake, probably Kyoto, 1800 to 1850; banquet sequence of white, red and black; butterflies symbolise harmony
Japanese usually hold Shinto-style ceremonies and pronounce vows to the kami
Order of a grand Shinto rite: harae, norito, music and dance, evergreen branch offerings (general rite, framed as such)
Communion with the kami by drinking offered sake after a festival
Kuniyoshi print The Wedding Colour Alteration Ceremony, 1843 to 1847
Smartraveller Japan: Exercise normal safety precautions; Reconsider your need to travel for Fukushima restricted areas
Heat waves July to September; typhoon season May to November, peak July to September
Visa-free up to 90 days; conditions can change; entry status cannot change without leaving
Overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia but in most cases is recognised
CNI commonly required; some authorities accept only locally issued CNIs
Embassies and consulates issue CNIs; fees apply
Tokyo Embassy and Osaka Consulate-General notarial by appointment; mail from within Japan only; mailed CNI must be witnessed
Sembazuru orikata (1797), one of the earliest origami instruction books, linked cranes
Washoku inscribed by UNESCO for New Year celebrations (section 6)
San-san-kudo shared cups carry a promise made before the kami (meaning as fact)
Parents' sake 'seals the bond' between families (meaning as fact)
